title: JANUS Axle Coin: two-sided print-in-place laurel gimbal for Bambu Lab A1
mission: Preserve the supplied two-sided JANUS coin relief inside a movable concentric-gimbal fidget while keeping the authoritative axle, socket and clearance geometry mechanically unchanged.

design_contract.central_medallion: Direct topology-preserving transfer of the supplied JANUS_Coin(4) relief.
design_contract.outer_orbit: Recessed Greek-key/meander band and external crown teeth.
design_contract.middle_orbits: Raised antique laurel bas-relief with central veins and framing cuts on both faces.
design_contract.motion: Three nested orbit interfaces plus a captive rotating central medallion.

repository_materials.binary_distribution_reason: The mechanism source embeds MakerWorld Standard Digital File License metadata; public redistribution of a derivative digital model requires a separate permission check.

mechanical_validation.critical_repair: The earlier ornament mask protected only each ring's nominal axis and reduced a neighbouring interface clearance to about 0.12 mm. v2.5 protects every axle diameter touched by each ring and restores all authoritative source clearances.

supports.purpose: Support the lower arcs and the central medallion while remaining too wide to enter the 0.20–0.31 mm mechanism gaps.

confirmed: The 3MF container is structurally valid under ZIP/XML/JSON checks.
The final geometry is self-contained and does not use external production components.
The decorated mesh preserves the measured source clearances and leaves all protected interface vertices unchanged.
Both ring faces contain the same laurel and Greek-key decoration policy.
not_yet_confirmed: Successful end-to-end Bambu Studio slicing on the user's workstation.
Successful physical print and clean support removal.
Long-term wear, fatigue and repeated-motion durability.
